claims_supported: PouchDB/CouchDB expose immediate 409 revision conflicts and eventual same-document conflicts.
For offline same-document divergent revisions, default winner selection is deterministic but arbitrary; losing revisions remain addressable and applications choose handling.
Append-only delta documents can reduce edit conflicts but do not alone enforce ferry capacity across terminals.

claims_supported: Local and remote PouchDB databases can replicate bidirectionally.
Live replication can retry after network errors when configured with live and retry; paused/active states are exposed.
The guide describes multi-master eventual consistency and a deterministic conflict winner.

sources.version_status: Rolling official docs, last updated 2026-10-07 UTC; SDK version is not fixed by the page, examples include Web modular SDK v9 and legacy API.
sources.locator: “Access data offline”, “Configure offline persistence”, Web cache examples, and offline queries; observed lines 450-505 and 583-585.
sources.access_timestamp_note: Source retrieval completed no later than this timestamp; page itself reports last updated 2026-10-07 UTC.
observed_operations: web search for official Firestore offline documentation
claims_supported: Firestore caches actively used data and syncs local changes on reconnect; multiple changes to the same document use last-write-wins.
Web persistence is disabled by default; its cache is not automatically cleared between sessions and is supported only in Chrome, Safari, and Firefox.
Offline queries see cached data only and may return empty results when matching data was never cached; automatic offline-query indexing is disabled by default.

claims_supported: Transactions are atomic and retried after concurrent edits, but fail while client is offline.
A client-side offline queue is therefore not equivalent to an offline capacity reservation transaction.
Document/rule and transaction limits need workload-specific validation.

claims_supported: Standard Firestore lists daily free quotas of 50,000 reads, 20,000 writes, 20,000 deletes, 1 GiB stored data, and 10 GiB monthly outbound transfer for the qualifying database.
Paid usage depends on reads, writes, deletes, index reads, storage, and bandwidth; a cost estimate needs region and workload.
